web_evidence.title: Norse Mythology — Bloomsbury edition preview
web_evidence.note: The authorized edition preview distinguishes Gaiman's signed, first-person introduction from 'The Players' and the opening myth, where Odin, Thor, Loki, and Surtr are narrated externally in third person.

web_evidence.title: Neil Gaiman Writing Styles in Norse Mythology (Stories)
web_evidence.note: Its point-of-view analysis explicitly states that the book generally maintains third-person omniscient narration, with focal attention shifting among Loki, Odin, and Thor.

web_evidence.title: Omniscient Point of View: Benefits and Pitfalls
web_evidence.note: An editor identifies Norse Mythology as omniscient narration and analyzes an interior passage from 'Mimir's Head and Odin's Eye' in which the narrator externally reports multiple characters' responses.

web_evidence.title: REVIEWED: Norse Mythology
web_evidence.note: The review explicitly describes a third-person narrator linking events across the fifteen tales and making them resemble one continuous episodic story.

person_note: The myth-tale body uses a nonparticipating third-person storyteller, often with omniscient access to different gods' thoughts and feelings. Multiple Goodreads passages from separate tales expose that position, and the authorized early-book preview plus explicit whole-book and interior analyses agree. First-person passages in the sample belong to Gaiman's signed introduction or to character dialogue, while apparent second person is reader address or generic phrasing rather than sustained narration of a protagonist. No credible evidence indicates sustained first- or second-person tale sections; the only scope limitation is that the Tier A preview covers the introduction and early sections rather than the entire book.
